summary: This clipped Microsoft Learn note documents the SharePointOnlineCredentials class in the Microsoft.SharePoint.Client namespace, which provides credentials for accessing SharePoint Online resources. It covers the class declaration and thread safety, the constructor taking a username and SecureString password, and the members list: the UserName property, the GetAuthenticationCookie and GetCredential methods, and the ExecutingWebRequest event. Most of the text is repeated navigation, cookie banner and footer boilerplate.
one_line: Microsoft Learn API reference for the SharePointOnlineCredentials class, its constructor, members, and authentication cookie methods.
key_facts: SharePointOnlineCredentials represents an object that provides credentials to access SharePoint Online resources.
SharePointOnlineCredentials is in the Microsoft.SharePoint.Client namespace and the Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.Runtime assembly (Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.Runtime.dll).
The class is declared as Public NotInheritable Class in Visual Basic and as public sealed class in C#, and implements ICredentials.
Any public static (Shared in Visual Basic) members of SharePointOnlineCredentials are thread safe; instance members are not guaranteed to be thread safe.
The SharePointOnlineCredentials constructor takes a username parameter of type System.String and a password parameter of type System.Security.SecureString.
The UserName property gets the user name associated with the credentials passed in the SharePointOnlineCredentials constructor.
The GetAuthenticationCookie(Uri) method gets the authentication cookie.
The GetAuthenticationCookie(Uri, Boolean) overload is also listed in the method overload list.
The GetCredential method gets the network credentials with the specified URI and authentication type.
ToString is listed as a method inherited from System.Object.
The ExecutingWebRequest event is listed under the class's events.
The class's inheritance hierarchy is System.Object followed by Microsoft.SharePoint.Client.SharePointOnlineCredentials.
